text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Jurong Town Corp unveils initiative to make more productive use of industrial land.
- Thai Cabinet bites bullet and approves economic bailout plan by International Monetary Fund -- including credit line of at least US$1.5 billion -- to help keep economy afloat.
- About 180 elderly workers wait in vain for an hour at underground carpark to be paid July wages by their employers.
- Former Merrill Lynch broker Kevin Wallace expected to seek permission from Hongkong police and judiciary to travel to Singapore to face court.
- Tycoon Li Ka-shing takes S$540 million stake in Hongkong's grandest "hong", Jardine Matheson Holdings, and its property unit Hongkong Land -- both listed on Singapore bourse.
- Applications for Housing Board resale flats hit record 11,677 in second quarter as prices continue to fall -- although by mere 1 percent.

- Government draws up plans to stretch supply of industrial land by building taller factories and warehouses, redeveloping older industrial estates en-bloc, and raising production efficiency on industrial land.
- Singapore-based hydraulic systems maker and distributor Zicom Pte Ltd plans to list its shares on Stock Exchange of Singapore within next two years.
- Haw Par and Singapore Technologies Industrial Corp are planning to develop aquarium theme park in Chengdu, capital of China's Sichuan province.
- Investors greet Aztech Systems' new 96-voice sound card product with initial burst of enthusiasm, driving stock to intra-day high of 65 cents from 58.5 cents in first hour of trading.
- Bus operator SBS ventures into new business with opening of motor workshop at Bradell Road premises.
- Punters continue to take profits on Venture Manufacturing following company's cautious comments on what new Novastation software could do for bottomline.
